name: Baklava
subtitle: From Ginger
equipment: Blender, jelly roll size sheet, sharp chef knife, wax paper
notes: At the 2012 TCA meet, one taster declared, “This is the best thing I have ever tasted!” Best if eaten within 24 hours of baking. Not likely to last much longer anyway unless you have a very good hiding spot.

items: 1 box phyllo dough (generally purchased in the freezer section), thawed
½ cup butter for each half of the dough

steps.title: Make the filling
steps.body: Prepare filling in blender, until fine: **1½ cups nuts** (walnuts or pecans), **¾ cup sugar** and **½ tsp cinnamon**.

steps.title: Prepare the phyllo
steps.body: Using **1 box phyllo dough** (generally purchased in the freezer section), thawed, and cut in half, work with one half of dough at a time, keep the second covered to retain moisture (modern phyllo dough already comes split in two packages per box). Place dough on a jelly roll size sheet.

steps.title: Add the filling
steps.body: Remove the top half of the layers, and spread half of the nut/sugar filling mixture over the dough. Replace the top layers, and using a sharp chef knife, cut into 2-inch squares, then each square in half to make triangles.

steps.title: Butter the triangles
steps.body: Drizzle over cut triangles: **½ cup butter**.

steps.title: Repeat for the second half
steps.body: Repeat for the second half of the dough, using the remainder of the filling, and another **½ cup butter**.

steps.title: Bake
steps.body: Bake for 20 minutes at 325°F, then for about 20 more minutes at 300°F, until golden brown—not too dark, but not too light.

steps.title: Make the syrup
steps.body: Prepare syrup by boiling for 1 minute: **½ cup water** and **1½ cups sugar**. Add **½ tsp lemon juice**.

steps.title: Drizzle the syrup
steps.body: Drizzle half of syrup over each pan of cookies as it comes out of the oven. Remove baklava to wax paper before sugar cools.
